item: R2 RMD (Relative Mahalanobis Distance), one round, CPU on cached Phase 13 features

score.MD_k: class-conditional Mahalanobis, paper standard: class means on ISIC train, shared pooled within-class covariance /(N-K) + 1e-3 I
score.MD_0: single Gaussian on ISIC train ignoring labels: global mean, full covariance /(N-1) + 1e-3 I
score.detector_score: min_k RMD_k(z); higher = more OOD; AUROC with OOD as positives
score.fit_data: ISIC train only; no OOD or domain data in any statistic

representations.primary: z_lesion_norm (16-d; the paper's z_lesion, the representation in Table 1)

evaluation_sets.id_primary: full ISIC test (n=5067), as in the paper
evaluation_sets.runs: all 27 Phase 13 runs: lambda in {0,0.25,0.5,1,2,4,8}, 5 seeds at {0,2,8}, 3 elsewhere
evaluation_sets.report: mean +/- s.d. across seeds per lambda, MD and RMD side by side

prediction.quantity: f = (AUROC_RMD - AUROC_MD) / (0.5 - AUROC_MD) at lambda=2, mean over 5 seeds, z_lesion_norm, ID full: the fraction of the below-chance gap (the inversion) that RMD removes
prediction.collapse_not_repaired: AUROC_RMD(lambda=2) <= 0.60 on both OOD sets (vs MD at lambda=0: 0.843 / 0.764)
prediction.rationale: Item 2: at lambda=2 OOD collapses toward the NV centroid; NV is the majority class, so the label-free Gaussian MD_0 is also centred near NV and subtracting it partly cancels the NV pull on OOD. It removes no information the encoder discarded, so it cannot restore lambda=0 separability.

outcomes.f >= 1 (inversion fully removed) and AUR: RMD repairs more than the inversion: report as contradicting the prediction
outcomes.0.25 <= f <= 0.75: as predicted: partial removal of the inversion, collapse remains
outcomes.f < 0.25: RMD does not remove the inversion

required_caveat: RMD applies only to Mahalanobis. kNN, MSP, Energy and cosine also collapsed with lambda and have no RMD analogue; whatever RMD recovers is a partial fix of the monitoring failure, not a fix.
standing_rules: one round; no retuning of eps, representation or score after seeing results; failures reported as findings
